prompt: Finish the checked exception RuleViolation so it formats itself as "field: reason", throw it from SignupValidator for the first broken rule, and have SignupBatchProcessor catch it so a bad sign-up is recorded instead of stopping the batch.
explanation: A custom exception is just a class that extends Exception and can carry extra data -- here the field name, which a plain message string would have buried. Because RuleViolation is checked, validate must declare throws RuleViolation and every caller has to deal with it. The batch processor deals with it by catching: the try block counts a success and the catch block records the failure, so one bad row never ends the run.
hints: Overriding getMessage() is enough to change how the exception prints -- keep the field and reason in their own fields.
Check the rules in the order given and throw immediately, so a sign-up that breaks two rules only reports the first.
In submit, put the validate call and the accepted++ inside the try; the counter only increases when no exception was thrown.
